intro.say: Some things will surely happen, and some can never happen. Let us decide!

rounds.say: Certain means it will surely happen. The sun will rise tomorrow morning. That is certain!
rounds.caption: Certain ✅

rounds.say: Impossible means it can never happen. A cat will never lay an egg. That is impossible!
rounds.caption: Impossible ❌

rounds.ask: A fish will climb up a tree. Certain or impossible?

options.label: Certain
options.why: Fish do not have legs to climb with.

rounds.explain: Fish live in water and cannot climb trees.

rounds.ask: After Monday comes Tuesday. Certain or impossible?

options.label: Impossible
options.why: Tuesday always comes after Monday.

rounds.explain: Every week, Tuesday comes right after Monday.

rounds.ask: This bag has only red balls. You pick one. Will it be red?

options.label: Impossible
options.why: There is nothing else in the bag.

rounds.explain: Every ball is red, so you will surely pick red.

rounds.ask: Same bag of red balls. Will you pick a blue ball?

options.label: Certain
options.why: The bag only has red balls.

rounds.explain: There are not any blue balls, so it is impossible.

rounds.ask: You drop a ball. Will it fall down?

options.label: Impossible
options.why: Things always fall down when we let go.

rounds.explain: When you let go, things always fall down.

rounds.ask: A dog will grow wings and fly. Certain or impossible?

options.label: Certain
options.why: Dogs can never grow wings.

rounds.explain: Dogs do not have wings, so it is impossible.

intro.say: Some things might happen. Likely means it probably will. Unlikely means it probably will not.

rounds.say: Five red balls and one blue ball. If you pick without looking, red is likely. Blue is unlikely.
rounds.caption: Red: likely   Blue: unlikely

rounds.say: When there are the same number of each colour, they have the same chance.
rounds.caption: Same chance

rounds.ask: You pick one without looking. Which colour will you probably get?

options.label: Yellow
options.why: There is only one yellow.

rounds.explain: There are many more blue balls, so blue is likely.

rounds.ask: Same bag. Will you pick yellow?

options.label: Certain
options.why: There are lots of blue balls too.

options.label: Impossible
options.why: There is one yellow, so it could happen.

rounds.explain: There is only one yellow, so it could happen, but it is unlikely.

rounds.ask: Which colour has the better chance?

options.label: Green
options.why: Count them: 4 of each.

options.label: Red
options.why: Count them: 4 of each.

rounds.explain: There are 4 green and 4 red, so they have the same chance.

rounds.ask: You roll a dice. Will you roll a 6?

options.label: Likely
options.why: There are 6 numbers, and only one is a 6.

options.label: Impossible
options.why: A dice does have a 6.

rounds.explain: A dice has 6 numbers. Only one of them is 6, so it is unlikely.

rounds.ask: The sky is full of dark grey clouds. Will it rain?

options.label: Impossible
options.why: Rain can come from dark clouds.

options.label: Unlikely
options.why: Dark clouds often bring rain.

rounds.explain: Dark clouds often bring rain, so rain is likely.

rounds.ask: This spinner has 3 shaded parts and 1 white part. Where will it probably land?

options.label: White
options.why: There is only 1 white part.

rounds.explain: There are more shaded parts, so shaded is likely.

intro.say: Let us use numbers to decide how likely something is. Count, compare and think!

rounds.say: A dice has 6 numbers, 1 to 6. Each number has the same chance. So rolling a 2 is unlikely, but rolling a number from 1 to 6 is certain.
More of something means more chance. 2 red, 5 blue, 1 green. Blue is most likely, green is least likely.
rounds.caption: Most: 🔵   Least: 🟢

rounds.ask: Roll a dice. Will you get a number less than 7?

options.label: Likely
options.why: Think: is there any number on a dice that is 7 or more?

options.label: Unlikely
options.why: Every number on a dice is less than 7.

options.label: Impossible
options.why: Every number on a dice is less than 7.

rounds.explain: Every number on a dice, 1 to 6, is less than 7, so it is certain.

rounds.ask: Roll a dice. Will you get a 7?

options.label: Certain
options.why: A dice only goes up to 6.

options.label: Likely
options.why: A dice only goes up to 6.

options.label: Unlikely
options.why: A dice does not have a 7 at all.

rounds.explain: A dice only has 1 to 6, so a 7 is impossible.

rounds.ask: Roll a dice. Will you get a number bigger than 1?

options.label: Certain
options.why: You could still roll a 1.

options.label: Unlikely
options.why: Five of the six numbers are bigger than 1.

options.label: Impossible
options.why: 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are bigger than 1.

rounds.explain: Five of the six numbers are bigger than 1, but you could roll a 1, so it is likely.

rounds.ask: How many blue balls must we add so red and blue have the same chance?

options.why: Then there would be 4 blue, not 5.
Then there would be 8 blue. Too many!

rounds.explain: Three blue and two more make five, the same as red.

rounds.ask: This spinner has 8 parts, and 2 are shaded. Is landing on shaded likely or unlikely?

options.label: Likely
options.why: Most of the parts are white.

options.label: Impossible
options.why: There are some shaded parts, so it can happen.

rounds.explain: Only 2 of the 8 parts are shaded, so it is unlikely.

rounds.ask: Put these in order, from impossible to certain.
rounds.explain: A cow flying is impossible, a 6 is unlikely, 1 to 5 is likely, and the sun rising is certain.
rounds.hint: Start with the thing that can never happen.
